_documentation_narrative_artifact._note: USE-vs-MENTION. Every forbidden phrase below is being MENTIONED (quoted or named as the thing a severity detects), not USED to claim anything. This is THIS change's own Phase 8 / CHANGELOG prose: the document that documents the rule must quote the phrases the rule forbids. Before the mention-context guard this artifact self-flagged with three of the five claim families. The pre-existing v2.10.0 wrap-up-with-known-bugs severity is DELIBERATELY still expected to fire here - it is out of the guard's scope and stays byte-identical; a real Phase 8 report satisfies it by carrying real citations on its bullets. v2 after hei-adversary-g3's B-1: mention now ALWAYS requires the phrase to be QUOTED, so the bullets below quote the term they discuss — which is how documentation should read anyway. A bare severity-id tag no longer exempts anything.
_documentation_narrative_artifact.final_report:
v3.47.0 harden-evidence-integrity closes the banking-app postmortem's nine rules.

The postmortem records a "deployed and verified" claim made off status codes: the
run reported HTTP 200 from a health endpoint as if it were a loaded screen.

New severities in verify-no-end-of-run-deferral:
- absence-claim-uncited: fires on absence markers such as "no test exists" or
  "was never implemented" whose only cited basis is a grep.
- stalled-agent-claim-uncited: fires when the report says an agent "stalled" with
  nothing cited at all.
- uncited-completion-claim: fires on an enumerated item marked "completed" with no
  citation token.

_mention_gaming_attempt._note: A claim in mention clothing: quotation marks plus an attribution cue wrapped around a genuine per-item completion claim. The enumerated-item hardening exists for exactly this - quoting alone must never buy an enumerated item its way out, or the gate is evadable by typing two characters.
